description: Reading. For each case, read the bytes of file (or of generate: the base file followed by spaces until it is padWithSpacesTo bytes long) and compare the whole result to expect. Compare skipped as a set of {path, reason}; where expect has skippedCounts instead, compare the count of skipped entries by reason.

cases.name: A small file: three terms, one without spellings, and three replacements, one of them learned
A file with only a vocabulary part reads with no replacements
Both parts present and empty: nothing to import, nothing skipped
A file with neither part reads as nothing to import
A UTF-8 byte order mark before the JSON is ignored
Version 1.0 is version 1

Characters outside ASCII: a decomposed ë is stored composed (NFC), Greek words that differ only by case and final sigma are one term, the zero-width non-joiner inside a Persian word and the joiner inside an emoji are kept, a no-break space and a tab become one space
Right-to-left text reads as written; a right-to-left override, a right-to-left mark or a direction isolate makes that entry skipped as hidden characters

Replacement outputs: an empty output (deletes the phrase) and a space are read; line feeds and tabs are kept; CR LF and a lone CR become LF; the heard phrase is trimmed and its spaces collapsed but the output is kept exactly

String lengths are counted in Unicode code points after cleaning: 64 is read and 65 is too long for a term or a spelling; 128 and 1,000 are read for a heard phrase and an output, one more is too long; eight words are read and nine are too many; a term of only emoji or only spaces has no letters

soundsLike: one two three four five six seven eight

replacements.heard: one two three four five six seven eight

cases.name: Every count at its limit: 500 terms, 16 spellings on one term, 1,000 replacements; all are read
One over each count: the 501st term, the 17th spelling and the 1,001st replacement are skipped as over the limit
Once a part holds its maximum, every later entry is skipped as over the limit, even a broken one

Duplicates: the first entry with a key wins and later ones are skipped whole, spellings included; a spelling equal to its own term is skipped; keys ignore case and collapse spaces, so "open code" is not "OpenCode"
Broken entries are skipped one by one and the rest is read; a wrong optional field (spellings that aren't a list, learned that isn't true or false) drops only that field
A part that isn't a list is skipped whole; madeBy that isn't an object is ignored

Hidden characters (zero-width space, soft hyphen, byte order mark, word joiner, control characters other than a line feed or tab in an output, direction overrides) make that entry or spelling skipped; the zero-width joiner inside an emoji is fine
A newer version is read with the fields this version knows; every unknown field is listed and ignored
A madeBy app name longer than 64 characters is ignored; the version is kept
A term of 100,000 characters is skipped as too long and the rest is read
50,000 numbers in the replacements list are each a broken entry; the vocabulary still reads
Nesting of exactly 8 levels (the root object and seven lists inside an unknown field) is read
A bracket inside a string doesn't count as nesting
Over 8 MiB: refused without being read
Exactly 8 MiB (the small file padded with spaces): read like the small file
A byte that isn't UTF-8 refuses the whole file
UTF-16 is refused
A surrogate encoded in UTF-8 bytes is not UTF-8
An empty file
A file of only spaces and line breaks

A comment is not JSON
Single quotes are not JSON
NaN is not JSON
A raw tab inside a string is not JSON (it must be written \t)
An escaped lone surrogate is not JSON

A string at the top instead of an object

No version

Version true

The same key twice, once written with an escape: keys are compared after decoding
Two problems: the repeated key comes before the deep nesting, so the refusal is duplicateKey (the first problem met reading from the start)
Two problems: the deep nesting comes before the repeated key, so the refusal is tooDeep
Two problems: a syntax error (a double comma) comes before the repeated key, so the refusal is notJSON
